components.cost_effect: Three derivative-block evaluations after separately charged inner solves.
components.goal: Evaluate the exact penalty value gradient using first derivatives once both exact inner minimizers are supplied.
components.key_estimate: thm.P058.penalty_gradient_bias gives h=grad L_lambda*(x) and ||h-grad F(x)||<=C_lambda/lambda; independent acceptance of the revised local argument is required.
components.name: Penalty gradient difference
components.operation: Combine the three gradient blocks specified in variant selected.
components.requires: Exact y* and y_lambda*, exact derivative blocks and the complete regularity conditions of the connected Theorem.
transfer_checks: Re-establish error bounds for approximate minimizers.
Establish sampling, dependence and variance properties for stochastic implementations.
Re-establish tracking and tuning for changing lambda.

limitations.statement: The component requires supplied exact minimizers and gives no finite first-order procedure for obtaining them.
Finite inner-solve work, approximate tracking errors, stochastic implementation and full Algorithm 1 convergence are outside this extracted component.

performance_links.scope_note: Exact-input deterministic gradient identity and pointwise bias only; fixed revision is bound through the same-batch structured performance link. This is not an inner-solve or convergence guarantee.

variants.cost: Given exact minimizers: one x-gradient evaluation of f and two x-gradient evaluations of g, plus vector subtraction, scaling and addition. All work obtaining the minimizers is separately charged and has no finite bound in this component. These are requested derivative-block counts, not a universal Oracle API cost. No Hessian query is used by this evaluation stage.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.4 Lemma 3.1; complete stochastic Algorithm 1 is outside this component's extracted implementation.
variants.name: Exact inner-minimizer evaluation
variants.output: h=grad L_lambda*(x); its Euclidean distance from grad F(x) is at most C_lambda/lambda under the connected Theorem's complete conditions.
variants.query_and_update: Evaluate a=grad_x f(x,y_lambda*), b=grad_x g(x,y_lambda*), c=grad_x g(x,y*); return h=a+lambda(b-c). This component has no outer iterate update.
variants.requirements: Definitions and Assumptions 1–2 in thm.P058.penalty_gradient_bias, plus exact evaluations of grad_x f and grad_x g at the specified points. Exact minimizers are supplied inputs, not first-order Oracle outputs.
variants.state_and_initialization: Stateless evaluation at supplied x and lambda with two supplied exact inner minimizers; no iterative initialization is needed for this component.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: One evaluation at fixed supplied positive lambda meeting the threshold; return after the three gradient blocks. No inner solver or iterative stopping rule is specified. The connected Theorem supplies the exact-input deterministic bias bound.

checked_locators: PDF pp.2–4 definitions, Assumptions and Lemma 3.1
use_restrictions: Reference scope is the exact-input evaluation component. The connected revised Theorem requires independent complete_local_argument_checked; no acceptance or publication is claimed.
Do not treat the supplied minimizers as free first-order Oracle results. Inner-solve work is charged separately without a finite bound here.
No unrestricted Oracle Complexity or complete F2SA convergence guarantee. Publish only with the accepted dependency-closed subset.

links.note: Same-batch deterministic exact-input identity and bias support. Publisher must bind the accepted Theorem revision; Algorithm acceptance depends on acceptance of that revised Theorem.

summary: Stateless exact-inner-minimizer gradient-evaluation component with three derivative-block evaluations and separately charged inner solves; its deterministic bias is connected to the same-batch Theorem pending independent acceptance.
title: Exact penalty-gradient component from first-order derivative differences
use_when: Separate penalty-gradient evaluation from the cost and error of obtaining inner minimizers.
